languages_frameworks: Groq SDK (groq==1.7.0, OpenAI gpt-oss / qwen models)

implemented_capabilities.capability: Graph-based root-cause ranking from active alerts
implemented_capabilities.notes: A firing-alert service is a root-cause candidate only if no alerting service is among its transitive dependencies (DEPENDS_ON*1..). Candidates are ranked by how many other alerting services depend on them (explains_count), then number of recent deploys, then name. Deploy recency uses a hard-coded clock constant NOW = 121 (minutes) rather than real time.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Blast radius, ownership, similar incidents, evidence path, incident creation
implemented_capabilities.notes: Parameterized ro_query reads; blast radius is unbounded reverse DEPENDS_ON*1.. with DISTINCT services ordered by tier; evidence path uses shortestPath(); create_incident deduplicates on an open incident for the same service and allocates INC-<n> ids in Cypher (read-modify-write, not concurrency safe).

implemented_capabilities.capability: Groq tool-calling agent with code-enforced answer validation
implemented_capabilities.notes: LLM is prompted with a fixed investigation order and an answer format, then code rewrites the first line, yes/no verdict and 'Suggested fix' line from the tool trace so facts cannot drift from the graph; nudges up to 3 times if get_evidence_path/create_incident are missing; falls back to a code-built answer if the model returns nothing. Includes a deterministic service_check mode that needs no LLM. Answer cache of 600 s.

The 'vector RAG' is a hand-written TF-IDF over one-sentence documents rendered from the same seed lists; the answer key is computed from the graph agent's own tools and checks (e.g. 'opens incident') the baseline structurally cannot do. The 10/10 vs 1/10 result is therefore illustrative, not an independent benchmark.

graph_models_and_cypher: FalkorDB graph 'incidents'. Labels: Service{name,tier}, Team, Engineer, Deploy{id,change,time}, Alert{id,message,severity,fired_at,status}, Incident{id,title,summary,status,opened_at}, Runbook. Edges: DEPENDS_ON, OWNS, MEMBER_OF, AUTHORED, DEPLOYED_TO, FIRED_ON, CAUSED_BY, RESOLVED, FIXED_WITH. ~25 services in a hand-authored shop topology. Plain openCypher with unbounded variable-length DEPENDS_ON*1.. and shortestPath; no APOC/GDS/algo procedures; all values are bound parameters.
algorithms: Alert-set root-cause elimination: exclude alerting services that depend (transitively) on another alerting service; rank by explained-alert count then deploy count (tools.py:find_root_cause)
Unbounded reverse transitive closure for blast radius (tools.py:find_blast_radius)
Code-side answer repair from tool trace (agent.py:fix_first_line, fix_yes_no, fix_suggested_fix)
Lightweight TF-IDF retrieval for the baseline (baseline.py:VectorIndex)
backend_interfaces: Python modules (tools.py, agent.py:ask/investigate) and CLI entry points (python agent.py, compare.py, load_data.py --reset); no HTTP API
frontend_interfaces: Streamlit app (app.py): alerts panel, Graphviz dot dependency view, diagnosis panel, KPI strip, 'Compare with vector RAG' toggle; LLM text is HTML-escaped (html.escape) before unsafe_allow_html rendering
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: Single tool-calling agent loop (MAX_STEPS 12, 3 nudges) with a model fallback chain across Groq models and quota handling; history of past incidents in the graph (Incident-CAUSED_BY-Service, RESOLVED, FIXED_WITH) is read as memory, and new incidents are written back, but there is no dedicated memory layer or multi-agent handoff.
tests_present: none (compare.py is an LLM-dependent evaluation script, not a test suite)
security_findings: agent.py:~28-30 - process exits at import if GROQ_API_KEY is unset; key read from env only (no hard-coded secret)

tools.py:~72-85 - create_incident computes the next INC id with a non-atomic read-then-create Cypher statement (race creates duplicate ids under concurrency); module-level _created dict in agent.py is process-local
tools.py - DEPENDS_ON*1.. traversals are unbounded; on a large or cyclic production graph this can blow up query time (no timeout or depth cap)
app.py - uses st.markdown(unsafe_allow_html=True) but wraps dynamic text in html.escape (esc); no eval/exec/subprocess/pickle found
agent.py:~215-235 - LLM tool-call arguments are JSON-parsed and dispatched only to a fixed FUNCTIONS allowlist; arbitrary Cypher is not exposed
duplicates_or_overlaps: Same RCA family as AgentAhmed/blast-radius (ROOT_CAUSE_CANDIDATES, blast radius, who-to-page, similar incidents) and KHARSHAVARDHAN-eng/CausalTrace; this repo is a smaller, simpler version with the best 'code overrides LLM answer' pattern.
evidence_drift_relevance: LOW - the trace-derived answer repair keeps stated facts consistent with tool outputs and incidents are deduplicated, but there is no provenance metadata, supersession, validity window or approval step; time is a hard-coded constant.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: Pure-Python post-processing that rebuilds or corrects key answer lines from the tool-call trace so LLM prose cannot contradict graph facts; portable to any tool-trace based agent.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: none for the repair functions; FalkorDB + Groq key for the surrounding agent

strategy_rationale: The RCA logic duplicates the stronger AgentAhmed/blast-radius implementation, uses a synthetic topology with a hard-coded clock, has no tests or license; only the trace-driven answer-repair pattern is worth copying as an idea.
